_: Codex's rung of the lane ladder. Paired name-for-name with .agents/lanes/claude.json: the same LN means the same *relative* capability on both harnesses, so a skill declares `lane: L4` once and each harness resolves it to its own model. These two files are the only two places in the repo a model name may appear. Rungs are ordered L1 (most capable) to L5 (cheapest).
$comment_skill_supports_effort: Whether this harness accepts an effort key in SKILL.md front matter. Codex does not, so a Codex skill payload gets the rung's model alone and the rung's effort reaches it only through a lane agent.

L1.summary: Irreversible work at the top of the ladder, where a mistake cannot be taken back.
L1.why: top family at the setting above `high`. For work whose mistake cannot be taken back: stored data shape, a published contract, a merge that lands.

L2.summary: Open-ended judgement at the top of the ladder, where the answer is not yet known.
L2.why: top family at its default setting. Open-ended judgement: architecture, plan authoring, a diagnosis with no known answer.

L3.summary: Ordinary specified work that a compiler or a test suite will catch.
L3.why: the workhorse. Specified work that a compiler or a test suite will catch: features, bugfixes, review lenses.

L4.summary: Mechanical work whose shape is already decided.
L4.why: the small family at its default setting. Mechanical work whose shape is already decided: scripted edits, docs, ledger upkeep.

L5.summary: Clerical work with a small input and no judgement to make.
L5.why: clerical work with a small input: commit, push, pull, sync, one poll. Codex has no family below `luna`, so this rung is the same model as L4 at the lowest setting -- an honest asymmetry with Claude, whose L5 drops a family.

$comment_context_ceiling: null means unrecorded, not unlimited. The Claude table carries real per-model windows from the published model table; the Codex figures are not verified here, so recording a number would be inventing one. A lane consumer that needs a ceiling must treat null as 'unknown' and not assume the input fits.
